headline: India 3, Bangladesh 0: Bangladesh U-20s crash out of Asian Cup qualifiers
summary: The Red-Green brigade suffered a heavy defeat against India, ending a disappointing campaign with three consecutive losses.
details: Bangladesh U-20s suffered a crushing 3-0 defeat against India in their final match of the AFC U-20 Asian Cup qualifiers at Dostlik Stadium.
The match was a culmination of a struggling campaign where Bangladesh lost all three of their group matches, including a 2-0 loss to Uzbekistan and a 3-0 loss to Syria.
India took the lead in the 26th minute when Danny Meitei Laishram scored after the Bangladeshi defense failed to clear the ball from the box.
The lead was doubled in the 60th minute by Vishal Yadav, who scored a stunning back-volley following a back-header from a throw-in.
The defeat was sealed with a third goal from substitute midfielder Mohammed Arbash late in the game, exploiting further defensive lapses.
The tournament was marked by turmoil, including the sacking of British coach Gerard Jones by BFF due to poor performance and off-field controversies.
Interim coach Atiqur Rahman took charge for the final match, but was unable to prevent the team's collapse on the field.
caption:
Three matches, three losses. Bangladesh U-20s exit the AFC Asian Cup qualifiers in heartbreaking fashion.

Bangladesh U-20s suffered a crushing 3-0 defeat against India in their final match of the AFC U-20 Asian Cup qualifiers at Dostlik Stadium.

The match was a culmination of a struggling campaign where Bangladesh lost all three of their group matches, including a 2-0 loss to Uzbekistan and a 3-0 loss to Syria.

India took the lead in the 26th minute when Danny Meitei Laishram scored after the Bangladeshi defense failed to clear the ball from the box.

The lead was doubled in the 60th minute by Vishal Yadav, who scored a stunning back-volley following a back-header from a throw-in.

The defeat was sealed with a third goal from substitute midfielder Mohammed Arbash late in the game, exploiting further defensive lapses.

The tournament was marked by turmoil, including the sacking of British coach Gerard Jones by BFF due to poor performance and off-field controversies.

Interim coach Atiqur Rahman took charge for the final match, but was unable to prevent the team's collapse on the field.

headline: Tk 1.29 lakh: Bangladesh’s per capita debt reaches new high
summary: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury reveals the current debt burden per person in parliament, outlining plans to reduce reliance on high-cost loans.
details: As of March 2026, Bangladesh's per capita debt has reached Tk 129,239, according to Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury during a parliamentary session.
To address this, the government is focusing on increasing revenue collection, improving public finance management, and implementing more disciplined debt management strategies.
The minister stated that initiatives are underway to expand tax and non-tax revenue (NTR) to reduce the necessity for borrowing and increase the government's own income.
Efforts are also being made to make public expenditure more economical and effective by controlling unnecessary and non-priority spending.
To lower interest rates and refinancing risks, the government is pursuing market-based credit expansion and enhancing the competitiveness of the government securities market.
The government is also working to develop the domestic credit market and expand the investor base to create a more balanced debt portfolio.
Additionally, limits are being applied to control excessive borrowing through savings certificates, aligning their rates with prevailing market conditions.
The government is now emphasizing the implementation of an Annual Borrowing Plan to prevent unplanned and excessive borrowing in the future.
caption:
Every single person in Bangladesh now carries a debt burden of Tk 1.29 lakh.

As of March 2026, Bangladesh's per capita debt has reached Tk 129,239, according to Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury during a parliamentary session.

To address this, the government is focusing on increasing revenue collection, improving public finance management, and implementing more disciplined debt management strategies.

The minister stated that initiatives are underway to expand tax and non-tax revenue (NTR) to reduce the necessity for borrowing and increase the government's own income.

Efforts are also being made to make public expenditure more economical and effective by controlling unnecessary and non-priority spending.

To lower interest rates and refinancing risks, the government is pursuing market-based credit expansion and enhancing the competitiveness of the government securities market.

The government is also working to develop the domestic credit market and expand the investor base to create a more balanced debt portfolio.

Additionally, limits are being applied to control excessive borrowing through savings certificates, aligning their rates with prevailing market conditions.

The government is now emphasizing the implementation of an Annual Borrowing Plan to prevent unplanned and excessive borrowing in the future.
